message.abstract:
<jats:p>
            This article discusses the relationship between two frameworks: universal composability (
            <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
              <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\(\mathsf{UC}\)</jats:tex-math>
            </jats:inline-formula>
            ) and robust compilation (
            <jats:italic>RC</jats:italic>
            ). In cryptography,
            <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
              <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\(\mathsf{UC}\)</jats:tex-math>
            </jats:inline-formula>
            is a framework for the specification and analysis of cryptographic protocols with a strong compositionality guarantee:
            <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
              <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\(\mathsf{UC}\)</jats:tex-math>
            </jats:inline-formula>
            protocols remain secure even when composed with other protocols. In programming language security,
            <jats:italic>RC</jats:italic>
            is a novel framework for determining secure compilation by proving whether compiled programs are as secure as their source-level counterparts no matter what target-level code they interact with. Presently, these disciplines are studied in isolation, though we argue that there is a deep connection between them and exploring this connection will benefit both research fields.
          </jats:p>
          <jats:p>
            This article formally proves the connection between
            <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
              <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\(\mathsf{UC}\)</jats:tex-math>
            </jats:inline-formula>
            and
            <jats:italic>RC</jats:italic>
            and then it explores the benefits of this connection (focussing on perfect, rather than computational
            <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
              <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\(\mathsf{UC}\)</jats:tex-math>
            </jats:inline-formula>
            ). For this, this article first identifies which conditions must programming languages fulfil in order to possibly attain
            <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
              <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\(\mathsf{UC}\)</jats:tex-math>
            </jats:inline-formula>
            -like composition. Then, it proves
            <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
              <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\(\mathsf{UC}\)</jats:tex-math>
            </jats:inline-formula>
            of both an existing and a new commitment protocol as a corollary of the related compilers attaining
            <jats:italic>RC</jats:italic>
            . Finally, it mechanises these proofs in DEEPSEC, obtaining symbolic guarantees that the protocol is indeed
            <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
              <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\(\mathsf{UC}\)</jats:tex-math>
            </jats:inline-formula>
            .
          </jats:p>
          <jats:p>
            Our connection lays the groundwork towards a better and deeper understanding of both
            <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
              <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\(\mathsf{UC}\)</jats:tex-math>
            </jats:inline-formula>
            and
            <jats:italic>RC</jats:italic>
            , and the benefits we showcase from this connection provide evidence of scalable mechanised proofs for
            <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
              <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\(\mathsf{UC}\)</jats:tex-math>
            </jats:inline-formula>
            .
          </jats:p>
title: Universal Composability Is Robust Compilation
